title: Browser rendering pipeline overview
learningObjectives: Explain browser rendering pipeline overview and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: A browser processes HTML into a DOM, CSS into style information, computes layout, paints visual output, and composites layers for display. JavaScript can trigger style recalculation, layout, paint, and compositing work depending on what it changes.
understand.whyItMatters: The pipeline explains layout shifts, rendering delays, and why repeated layout reads and writes can be expensive. Performance work should be measured in developer tools.
understand.analogy: Rendering is a production line that turns document structure and style rules into pixels on the screen.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The class change may cause style recalculation and subsequent rendering work depending on which CSS rules are affected.

examples.code: const panel=document.querySelector('#panel');panel?.classList.add('ready');// Browser schedules the required style and rendering work.
examples.explanation: The class change may cause style recalculation and subsequent rendering work depending on which CSS rules are affected.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Use the Performance panel to record a page interaction. Identify scripting, style, layout, paint, and compositing activity.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.

questions.prompt: Which browser stage calculates element positions and dimensions?
questions.explanation: Layout computes geometry such as element sizes and positions.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable web engineering habit?
options: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
Assume the browser always behaves exactly as expected
questions.answer: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
questions.explanation: Reliable web work combines standards knowledge with real testing and inclusive fallbacks.
